prompt: PaceCircle is a paid app that puts adults into four-person walking-accountability pods. During the past six months, 24 community-center events produced 1,800 attendees, 1,200 trial starts, 900 paid members, 720 people who joined a pod and logged three walks in their first seven days, 510 who were still logging a walk each week in week 8, and 190 who brought in another paying member. Those events cost $24,000 plus 520 founder hours: a founder hosts every kickoff and manually rematches quiet pods. A separate three-month creator campaign produced 2.4 million video views, 80,000 landing-page visits, 18,000 trials, 2,700 paid members, 810 people who reached the same first-week behavior, 72 who were active in week 8, and 9 paid referrals; it cost $45,000 and received no founder help. A corporate-benefits broker has offered a nonbinding, exclusive 90-day free pilot across 75 employers, with the eventual per-member fee still open. The team has not interviewed employees or benefits buyers in that channel. The CEO wants to buy a $250,000 creator bundle, replace community kickoffs with self-serve pod formation, announce the broker partnership, and hire four growth marketers. The board meets in 10 weeks, so one new cohort can reach the week-8 mark before the decision. Write the operating memo for the next 90 days: make the spending and partnership calls, specify what the team should run and measure before the board meeting, state the decisions that follow the evidence, and assign the follow-on work.
criteria: Treats the community-center adult-member segment as post-validation growth work because it has paid and retained use, while keeping the untested corporate-benefits channel under learning-from-users until employees or buyers supply discriminating behavioral or payment evidence; it does not treat the broker offer, exclusivity request, announcement, views, trials, or signups as demand validation.

Builds separate community and creator cohort paths from exposure through trial, payment, the explicit first-week pod-and-three-walk activation event, week-8 retained walking, and paid referral, using the supplied numerators and denominators plus cash cost, founder support, source, and plausible founder-assistance or channel-quality confounders; it identifies the creator cohort's activation-to-retention break before prescribing more acquisition.

Declines or defers the $250,000 creator commitment and broad self-serve replacement, and instead runs a bounded comparison that preserves the working founder-assisted community path while testing reduced or self-serve help, records rematching and other hidden founder rescue, and expands only if the loop works without that rescue.

Sets a calendar review after the new cohort can mature for eight weeks and precommits numeric pass, repair, and stop-or-pause thresholds covering activation, week-8 retention, and support burden or unit economics, with explicit branches for scaling, keeping the work manual, repairing the product or channel, and stopping the weak channel; raw reach or acquisition volume alone cannot trigger expansion.

Names downstream owners in the resulting branches: growth owns the channel/cohort decision, learning-from-users owns evidence for the new corporate segment, designing-business-models owns the broker's payer, fee, exclusivity, and partner economics, shipping-and-iterating-products owns self-serve exposure and rollback, and engineering-for-leverage owns instrumentation or automation only after the outcome and bounds are specified.
